L10800: distributions in a general framework, and spent too much time and energy on
L10801: it. In that year 1953 he was recruited by Bourbaki. But he only remained for
L10802: a few years: he lacked humor and had difficulty accepting Bourbaki’s criticism
L10803: which is customarily rather virulent, and he left.
L10804: Our friendship was deep. He often came to play the piano at my house. He
L10805: was naturally very kind, and was particularly affectionate with our housekeeper
L10806: Alice, who reminded him of his mother. He moved to Paris in 1953, then spent
L10807: a year in Brazil where he wrote something on topological vector spaces which
L10808: appeared in 1958. He lived alone and worked twenty-five or twenty-six hour
L10809: days, which had the effect of shifting his daytimes throughout the usual cycle,
L10810: so that sometimes he worked in the daytime and other times at night. It is indeed
L10811: a little-known peculiarity of some mammals to have a natural cycle which is
L10812: actually slightly longer than 24 hours. If you keep them in a lighted underground
L10813: room, their circadian rhythm reaches cycles from 25 to 27 hours. Their usual
L10814: 24-hour-a-day life is just an adaptation to the solar rhythm. This is why an
L10815: airplane trip to the west is not so difficult for most people, whereas a trip to
L10816: the east creates longer and deeper problems. Grothendieck’s underground room
L10817: was the hotel room where he worked.

L10882: Research
L10883: The discovery of distributions was one thing, writing it up was another. The
L10884: task I gave myself from the year I spent in Grenoble until the appearance of
L10885: the two books on distributions in 1950 and 1951 was to write up everything
L10886: completely. The two books together contain about four hundred pages. Naturally,
L10887: they contain some grand ideas, but also a large number of technical parts. In
L10888: fact, as I said before, I find the book too short. On the whole, though, it is well-
L10889: written. Generally, publications are not very time-resistant, and it is necessary to
L10890: rewrite them or have them rewritten. But the book on distributions has withstood
L10891: the test of time. I believe that for the most part, I introduced the best possible
L10892: definitions and proofs.
